item.title: Kimi K3 Pushes Open-Source Models to the Frontier's Doorstep
item.description: A BOCOM International analysis argues Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 — 2.8 trillion parameters, natively multimodal, with a 1-million-token window — sits on the Pareto frontier of cost and capability, trailing only top closed models while cutting per-task cost sharply.

item.title: Under Domestic Compute Constraints, iFLYTEK Turns to Engineering
item.description: At its August earnings call, iFLYTEK acknowledged domestic accelerators trail Nvidia's H200 by up to 5x on long-context training. Instead of waiting for hardware, it is optimizing architecture, operators, memory and frameworks — proving the approach with Spark X2-Flash on Huawei Ascend 910B.

item.title: Chang'e-7 Heads for the Moon in a New Chapter for China's Lunar Program
item.description: Chang'e-7 and its Long March 5 Y14 rocket are at the Wenchang pad for a south-pole mission combining orbiting, landing, roving and hopping. Its key goal is confirming water ice in permanently shadowed craters, with 21 payloads and seven international partners.

item.title: China's Satellite-Making Sprint: Inside Wenchang's 1,000-a-Year Super Factory
item.description: Wenchang's satellite super factory passed acceptance in June and will trial-produce with a designed annual capacity of 1,000 satellites — about four months of China's entire 2025 output. GeeSpace, GalaxySpace and MinoSpace show how assembly-line manufacture is replacing the slow 'island' model.

item.title: China's Humanoid Robots Are Getting Faster — and Smarter
item.description: Crowds packed the World Robot Conference while humanoid athletes sprinted 100 metres in 9.32 seconds. Unitree, AgiBot and Honor showcased faster, cheaper hardware, as ball-screw and reducer prices fell sharply and robot entertainment deals emerged.
